flashcard_questions.q: What is a pilgrimage in Christianity?
flashcard_questions.a: A journey to a place of special religious significance.

flashcard_questions.q: When did Bernadette Soubirous report her visions of the Virgin Mary at Lourdes?
Where is the pilgrimage town of Lourdes?
What do pilgrims hope to gain from the spring water at Lourdes?
About how many pilgrims visit Lourdes each year?
Who founded the monastery on Iona in 563 CE?
What does it mean that the Iona Community is ecumenical?
flashcard_questions.a: It welcomes Christians of every denomination to worship together.

flashcard_questions.q: What do pilgrims to Iona look for, unlike pilgrims to Lourdes?
flashcard_questions.a: A simple, prayerful retreat rather than miracles or healing.
The Incarnation — that God became human in Jesus Christ.

flashcard_questions.q: When do most Christians celebrate Christmas?
What did the angel tell the shepherds at Jesus’s birth?
flashcard_questions.a: “Today in the town of David a Saviour has been born to you.”

flashcard_questions.q: Why is Easter the most important Christian festival?
flashcard_questions.a: It celebrates the resurrection, the foundation of the whole Christian faith.

flashcard_questions.q: Which verse did St Paul write about faith without the resurrection?
flashcard_questions.a: “If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile” (1 Corinthians 15:17).

flashcard_questions.q: What does Maundy Thursday remember in Holy Week?
flashcard_questions.a: The Last Supper, when Jesus washed his disciples’ feet.

notes: 15 cards: 5 place/case-study facts (Lourdes, Iona), 3 term→definition (pilgrimage, ecumenical, Incarnation), 2 date recall, 2 belief→source (Luke 2:11, 1 Corinthians 15:17), 3 practice→meaning (Lourdes water, Palm Sunday, Maundy Thursday). Dropped the 70 recognised cures and the 7 January Orthodox date to stay at 15.
